Field guide · Columbus, sourced

Columbus

Ohio’s capital — the Short North, German Village & a great immigrant table

86 places · 62 sights · 24 to eat & drink · 8 areas · 33 sources · status last checked 2026-08-24

Downtown & Scioto Mile Short North, Victorian & Italian Village German Village & Brewery District University District, Clintonville & OSU Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop Suburbs Madison County

Downtown & Scioto Mile 23

  1. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Ohio Theatre

    The 'Official Theatre of the State of Ohio' — a lavishly gilded 1928 Spanish-Baroque movie palace on Capitol Square, saved from the wrecking ball in 1969 and declared a National Historic Landmark in 1977. CAPA runs it today, with free summer walking tours and 'Mighty Morton' organ demos.

    Your guide’s note Free guided tours on select summer Saturdays; otherwise a ticketed performance venue.

    39 E State St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia, CityScene Magazine (Columbus)

  2. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Ohio Statehouse

    Ohio's 1861 Greek Revival capitol on Capitol Square — free tours, the Statehouse Museum, and grounds dotted with monuments in the heart of downtown.

    1 Capitol Sq, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    COSI

    The Center of Science and Industry — a top-ranked U.S. science museum in an Arata Isozaki building on the Scioto riverfront, with giant hands-on exhibits and a dinosaur gallery.

    333 W Broad St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Experience Columbus, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Columbus Museum of Art

    Strong holdings of American and European modernism (including Columbus native George Bellows) in a 1931 Renaissance-revival building with a light-filled modern wing.

    480 E Broad St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Scioto Mile and Bicentennial Park

    Downtown's riverfront promenade — a 15,000-sq-ft interactive fountain, gardens and skyline views stretching along the Scioto from the Arena District to the Whittier Peninsula.

    233 Civic Center Dr, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    North Market

    Columbus's last true public market (est. 1876) — 30-plus merchants including the original Jeni's, Momo Ghar and Hoyo's, just off the Short North and Arena District.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  7. Must see · Ice Cream & Bakeries · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams — North Market

    Jeni Britton Bauer launched Jeni's at the North Market in 2002; the grassy-buttermilk base and inventive flavors (Brambleberry Crisp, Brown Butter Almond Brittle) that turned a Columbus stall into a national brand.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, Wikipedia

  8. Must see · Somali & East African · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Momo Ghar — North Market

    Phenomenal Himalayan dumplings that put Columbus's huge Nepali-Bhutanese community on the map; the jhol momo swim in a spiced sesame broth. Featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Experience Columbus

  9. Must see · Somali & East African · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Hoyo's Kitchen — North Market

    The friendly gateway to Columbus's Somali food scene (one of the largest Somali communities in the US): tender suqaar, crisp sambusas and rice served the traditional way with a banana. 'Hoyo' means mother.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Experience Columbus

  10. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Veritas

    Chef Josh Dalton's glass-kitchen tasting menu, reinvented every few months — repeatedly ranked Columbus's #1 restaurant since 2012.

    11 W Gay St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Wikipedia

  11. Must see · American & New American · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Wolf's Ridge Brewing

    The rare brewery that's also one of the city's best restaurants — award-winning beers (the coffee-and-vanilla Daybreak cream ale) alongside a serious downtown dining room.

    215 N 4th St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Experience Columbus

  12. Must see · Asian · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Lan Viet Market

    North Market's Northern Vietnamese stall from Khanh Le and his mother Lan Pham (a North Market staple since 2010; earlier known as Lac Viet) — a from-scratch pho broth simmered 24 hours and crisp, balanced banh mi.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Official site

  13. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Topiary Park

    The only park based on a painting: sculpted yews recreate Seurat's 'A Sunday on La Grande Jatte' — 54 people, boats and dogs — on the Old Deaf School Park grounds. Free.

    480 E Town St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia, Official site

  14. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    National Veterans Memorial and Museum

    The only congressionally designated national museum for veterans of every branch and era, in a sculptural 2018 concrete-arch building (Allied Works) on the Scioto's west bank, ringed by a memorial grove and rooftop sanctuary.

    300 W Broad St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia, Experience Columbus

  15. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    LeVeque Tower

    The 1927 Art Deco skyscraper that has defined the skyline for a century — 555 feet, now a hotel, lit in changing colors nightly.

    50 W Broad St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Wikipedia, COLUMBUSMAKESART

  16. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Grange Insurance Audubon Center and Scioto Audubon Metro Park

    A LEED-Platinum birding center on the restored Whittier Peninsula wetlands, plus a 35-ft outdoor climbing wall and downtown skyline views. Free.

    505 W Whittier St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks

  17. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Thurber House

    The restored home of humorist and New Yorker cartoonist James Thurber, now a literary center, museum and bookstore on a Jefferson Avenue historic row.

    77 Jefferson Ave, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  18. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Southern Theatre

    The oldest surviving theatre in central Ohio — opened 1896 as the 'Great Southern Fireproof Hotel and Opera House' after a run of downtown theatre fires, it hosted Sarah Bernhardt, Anna Pavlova and John Philip Sousa. CAPA restored it in a 14-month, $10M rebuild reopening in 1998.

    21 E Main St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  19. Worth the detour · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Columbus Commons

    A six-acre downtown green built on the footprint of the old City Center mall — a restored 1914 carousel, free summer concerts, a Thursday farmers market and 200+ free events a year. Free.

    Look for Free; carousel rides seasonal (Apr–Sep).

    160 S High St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Experience Columbus

  20. Deep cut · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Central Ohio Fire Museum

    A restored 1908 downtown engine house of hand-drawn, horse-drawn and early motorized fire apparatus, with a kids' play space and fire-safety tours.

    260 N 4th St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  21. Deep cut · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Union Station Arch at McFerson Commons

    The last surviving arch of Columbus's demolished 1897 Union Station (a Daniel Burnham design), rescued during the 1976 wrecking and re-erected as the centerpiece of the 2.2-acre McFerson Commons in the Arena District. Free.

    McFerson Commons, Nationwide Blvd, Arena District, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Wikipedia, The Columbus Dispatch

  22. Deep cut · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Columbus Metropolitan Library — Main Library

    The flagship of a system twice named National Library of the Year — its $30M 2016 daylight-flooded renovation (GUND Partnership), opening onto Topiary Park, won the Columbus Landmarks James B. Recchie Design Award. Free to wander.

    96 S Grant Ave, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Architect Magazine

  23. Closed — kept for the record · Soul, BBQ & Southern · Downtown & Scioto Mile

    Hot Chicken Takeover — CLOSED

    A Columbus original that launched at the North Market in 2014 and built a devoted following (and a social mission) around its Nashville hot chicken. All central-Ohio locations closed in September 2025 — kept here for the record.

    59 Spruce St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by NBC4, Columbus Underground

Short North, Victorian & Italian Village 7

  1. Must see · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Short North Arts District

    The gallery, restaurant and shopping spine on High Street between downtown and OSU, marked by its signature lit metal arches; monthly Gallery Hop has run since 1984.

    N High St (Goodale St to W 5th Ave), Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Experience Columbus, Official site

  2. Must see · Breweries & Bars · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Seventh Son Brewing

    One of Columbus's OG craft breweries (2013), a local institution in Italian Village with street-level and second-floor patios in a former auto garage.

    1101 N 4th St, Columbus, OH 43201

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, SHORTNORTH

  3. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    One Line Coffee — Short North

    Specialty roaster's showcase Short North bar with a pour-over station and small sample-roaster; works directly with small coffee farmers and cooperatives, and among the strongest in-city options for locally roasted single-origin beans.

    745 N High St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, Experience Columbus

  4. Worth the detour · Ice Cream & Bakeries · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Fox in the Snow Cafe

    Italian Village's scratch bakery and hand-poured-coffee darling since 2014; the gooey cinnamon roll and egg sandwich draw morning lines.

    1031 N 4th St, Columbus, OH 43201

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, Experience Columbus, BWNICK

  5. Worth the detour · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Goodale Park

    Columbus's oldest park (donated 1851) in Victorian Village — a pond, fountain and gazebo, and host of the summer ComFest gathering.

    120 W Goodale St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  6. Worth the detour · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Columbus Museum of Art at The Pizzuti

    CMA's contemporary satellite in a restored Short North building — rotating exhibitions drawn from Ron and Ann Pizzuti's globe-spanning collection of contemporary art.

    632 N Park St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  7. Deep cut · Short North, Victorian & Italian Village

    Italian Village

    The historic district just east of the Short North — brick worker cottages and the redeveloped Jeffrey Park, now home to Seventh Son and Fox in the Snow. Address is the landmark Jeffrey Manufacturing office building.

    224 E 1st Ave, Columbus, OH 43201

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Official site, Columbus Underground

German Village & Brewery District 7

  1. Must see · German · German Village & Brewery District

    Schmidt's Sausage Haus

    German Village institution since 1886 in a brick livery stable. The Bahama Mama smoked sausage was voted Columbus's official food; the world-famous jumbo cream puffs are the other reason to come.

    240 E Kossuth St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Wikipedia, BWNICK

  2. Must see · German Village & Brewery District

    The Book Loft of German Village

    A literary labyrinth of 32 rooms of discounted books in pre-Civil War buildings — one of the largest independent bookstores in the country.

    631 S 3rd St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · German Village & Brewery District

    German Village

    A 19th-century German immigrant neighborhood of brick-paved streets and Italianate cottages — the largest privately funded historic district on the National Register. Address is the German Village Society Meeting Haus.

    588 S 3rd St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · American & New American · German Village & Brewery District

    Lindey's

    German Village's see-and-be-seen bistro since 1981 — steaks, seafood and one of the most beloved leafy patios in America.

    169 E Beck St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, Experience Columbus

  5. Must see · American & New American · German Village & Brewery District

    Agni

    Chef Avishar Barua — a James Beard 'Best Chef: Great Lakes' semifinalist — cooks inventive, Bangladeshi-inflected New American on the German Village edge; a recent Columbus Monthly #1.

    716 S High St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, NBC4

  6. Worth the detour · German Village & Brewery District

    Schiller Park

    German Village's 23-acre green heart (est. 1867) — Columbus's second-oldest park, with a lake, the Umbrella Girl fountain, a bust of poet Friedrich Schiller and summer 'Actors' Theatre' Shakespeare. Free.

    1069 Jaeger St, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  7. Closed — kept for the record · Burgers & Diners · German Village & Brewery District

    The Thurman Cafe — CLOSED

    Family-owned since 1942 and home of the Thurmanator, a monster double burger loaded with ham, bacon and three cheeses. TEMPORARILY CLOSED after an April 2026 electrical fire; owners have vowed to rebuild — call ahead before visiting.

    183 Thurman Ave, Columbus, OH 43206

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, Wikipedia, 10TV

University District, Clintonville & OSU 14

  1. Must see · Asian · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Meshikou

    Columbus' pioneering ramen shop (Bethel Centre), routinely called the best ramen in the city — and named best in Ohio by a national food guide. Columbus Monthly ran a First Look, and it's covered on alt.eats.columbus and by creator Breakfast With Nick. Yelp 587 reviews / Google high-rated.

    1506 Bethel Rd, Columbus, OH 43220

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, CFA, BWNICK

  2. Must see · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Wexner Center for the Arts

    Ohio State's contemporary-art laboratory in Peter Eisenman's landmark 1989 Deconstructivist building — galleries, avant-garde film and performance at the campus's edge.

    1871 N High St, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Ohio Stadium (the Horseshoe)

    The 1922 horseshoe-shaped, 100,000-plus-seat home of Buckeyes football — an enduring icon of college-football gameday and a National Register landmark.

    411 Woody Hayes Dr, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  4. Must see · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Billy Ireland Cartoon Library & Museum

    The world's largest collection of cartoons and comics — original Calvin and Hobbes, Peanuts and Pogo art — in Ohio State's Sullivant Hall, with free rotating gallery exhibitions.

    1813 N High St, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  5. Must see · Burgers & Diners · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Preston's: A Burger Joint

    Chefs Matt Heaggans & Catie Randazzo's cult smash burger — Ohio beef, American cheese, pickles and special sauce. A James Beard Blended Burger Project entrant that graduated from pop-up to a beloved Clintonville brick-and-mortar next to Combustion Brewery.

    2973 N High St, Columbus, OH 43202

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, COLUMBUS MONTHLY

  6. Worth the detour · Asian · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    NE Chinese Restaurant

    University District specialist in Dongbei (Northeastern/Manchurian) Chinese cooking — a rare regional cuisine for the city, reviewed by Columbus Underground and Columbus Monthly ("Short Order") and written up by creator Breakfast With Nick. Google high-rated with real volume.

    2620 N High St, Columbus, OH 43202

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, COLUMBUS MONTHLY, BWNICK

  7. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Columbus Park of Roses

    A free 13-acre rose garden inside Clintonville's Whetstone Park — 11,000-plus roses across 350-plus varieties, at their peak in June.

    3901 N High St, Columbus, OH 43214

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  8. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    The Oval at Ohio State

    The 11-acre historic green at the heart of OSU's campus, framed by University Hall and Thompson Library and landscaped with Olmsted-brothers input — the campus 'living room.'

    181 S Oval Dr, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  9. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Olentangy Trail

    A 13-plus-mile paved riverside greenway from downtown's North Bank Park up through OSU and Clintonville to Worthington — the city's spine for cycling and running. Address is the southern North Bank Park trailhead.

    311 W Long St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Official site

  10. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Ohio History Center and Ohio Village

    The state history museum in a striking 1970 Brutalist building, with the adjacent Ohio Village recreating an 1890s town. Ohio Village is under phased restoration into the mid-2020s.

    800 E 17th Ave, Columbus, OH 43211

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  11. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Jack Nicklaus Museum

    A 24,000-sq-ft shrine to the Golden Bear — the Columbus-born golf legend — inside the OSU sports complex, tracing his record 18 major championships.

    2355 Olentangy River Rd, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  12. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Orton Geological Museum

    Ohio State's free natural-history gem inside the 1893 Romanesque Orton Hall (a National Historic Landmark built of Ohio stone) — a full Cretodus shark, a giant ground sloth and thousands of fossils and minerals.

    155 S Oval Mall, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  13. Worth the detour · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Studio 35 Cinema & Drafthouse

    Clintonville's beloved neighborhood movie house — opened 1938 as the Indianola Theatre, it's Columbus's oldest cinema and the last independent one left, famous as the first U.S. theater licensed to serve alcohol. Two screens, 40 taps and an in-house pizza kitchen.

    3055 Indianola Ave, Columbus, OH 43202

    Recommended by Official site, ARTHOUSE

  14. Deep cut · University District, Clintonville & OSU

    Chadwick Arboretum & Learning Gardens

    A 60-plus-acre living plant collection across OSU's campus — ornamental Learning Gardens, a conifer and hosta collection and a Chartres-style labyrinth. Open dawn to dusk, free.

    2001 Fyffe Ct, Columbus, OH 43210

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall 8

  1. Must see · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Franklin Park Conservatory and Botanical Gardens

    An 1895 glasshouse built for a world's fair, with themed biomes, a permanent Chihuly glass collection and blooming seasonal gardens on the near east side.

    1777 E Broad St, Columbus, OH 43203

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  2. Must see · Columbus-Style Pizza · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Rubino's Pizza

    A Bexley shrine since 1954: ultra-thin cracker crust, cash only, no alcohol, hand-written checks and folded paper 'tents' — Columbus-style pizza at its most austere and beloved.

    2643 E Main St, Bexley, OH 43209

    Recommended by COLUMBUS MONTHLY, 614 MAGAZINE

  3. Worth the detour · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Drexel Theatre

    Central Ohio's home for independent and international film — a 1937 Art Deco/Art Moderne neighborhood movie house in Bexley, on the National Register and running continuously since Christmas Day 1937.

    2254 E Main St, Bexley, OH 43209

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia, Columbus Association for the Performing Arts

  4. Worth the detour · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Kelton House Museum & Garden

    An 1852 Greek Revival/Italianate home on the near east side, a documented Underground Railroad stop, preserved with original Kelton-family furnishings and a period garden.

    586 E Town St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  5. Worth the detour · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Schumacher Gallery

    Capital University's free art museum on the top floor of its Bexley library — 3,000+ works spanning Rembrandt, Dürer, Goya, Renoir, Cassatt, Picasso, Chagall and Warhol, plus rotating exhibits of Indigenous and local artists.

    Your guide’s note Free; open during the academic year only (closed summers and university holidays).

    Blackmore Library, 4th Fl, 2199 E Main St, Bexley, OH 43209

    Recommended by Official site, COLUMBUSMAKESART

  6. Worth the detour · American & New American · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    TAT Ristorante di Famiglia

    Columbus's oldest Italian restaurant (est. 1929, 'Talk of the Town'), credited with serving the city's first pizza. Wood-paneled, red-sauce, old-world charm.

    1210 S James Rd, Columbus, OH 43227

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, 614 MAGAZINE

  7. Worth the detour · Asian · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Huong Vietnamese Restaurant

    Long-running Morse Rd Vietnamese room (murals, plastic fruit trees) singled out by Columbus Underground for a super-crunchy grilled-chicken banh mi and picked as a reviewers' favorite on alt.eats.columbus (Columbus Food Adventures). Google ~4.4 with high volume.

    1270 Morse Rd, Columbus, OH 43229

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, CFA

  8. Deep cut · Bexley, Olde Towne East & Whitehall

    Jeffrey Mansion

    A 1905 brick mansion built by Columbus mayor Robert H. Jeffrey, willed to Bexley in 1941 and now the centerpiece of a 40-acre park of woodland trails, an Alum Creek overlook and a pool.

    165 N Parkview Ave, Bexley, OH 43209

    Recommended by Official site, Experience Columbus

Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop 6

  1. Must see · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Battelle Darby Creek Metro Park

    A 7,000-plus-acre metro park on the state-and-national scenic Big and Little Darby Creeks — restored tallgrass prairie with a free-roaming bison herd, a nature center and miles of trail. Free.

    1775 Darby Creek Dr, Galloway, OH 43119

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Wikipedia, Experience Columbus

  2. Must see · American & New American · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Anthony-Thomas Candy Company

    Columbus's family chocolatier since 1952 and maker of the definitive Ohio buckeye — peanut-butter fudge dipped in chocolate. Free factory tours on the west side.

    1777 Arlingate Ln, Columbus, OH 43228

    Recommended by Wikipedia, SNACKANDBAKERY

  3. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Stauf's Coffee Roasters — Grandview

    Columbus's original micro-roaster and coffee house (founded 1988 in Grandview) — 60-plus small-batch coffees hand-selected from 20-plus countries, plus pastries and locally made desserts.

    1277 Grandview Ave, Columbus, OH 43212

    Recommended by Experience Columbus, CityScene Magazine (Columbus)

  4. Worth the detour · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Columbus Idea Foundry

    A 60,000-sq-ft Franklinton makerspace billed as the physically largest in the world — welding, blacksmithing, woodshop, 3D printing and 80+ classes a month, with free RSVP evening tours and demonstrations.

    Your guide’s note Free evening tours by RSVP; workshops/membership ticketed.

    421 W State St, Columbus, OH 43215

    Recommended by Official site, Experience Columbus, CityScene Magazine (Columbus)

  5. Worth the detour · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Green Lawn Cemetery

    Ohio's second-largest cemetery (est. 1848) — a 325-acre garden cemetery and registered arboretum with an old-growth oak forest, ornate mausoleums and an Audubon Important Bird Area; resting place of the Wright brothers' family and Eddie Rickenbacker.

    1000 Greenlawn Ave, Columbus, OH 43223

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  6. Deep cut · Franklinton, Grandview & Hilltop

    Camp Chase Confederate Cemetery

    A National Cemetery on the Hilltop holding 2,200-plus Confederate soldiers who died at the Union's Camp Chase prison — rows of white headstones behind a boulder arch reading 'Americans.' Free.

    2900 Sullivant Ave, Columbus, OH 43204

    Recommended by National Park Service, Wikipedia

Suburbs 18

Dublin, Worthington, Westerville, New Albany

  1. Must see · Suburbs

    Columbus Zoo and Aquarium

    One of America's premier zoos (Jack Hanna's longtime home base), north of the city in Powell, with the Zoombezi Bay water park next door.

    4850 W Powell Rd, Powell, OH 43065

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  2. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Field of Corn (Cornhenge)

    Malcolm Cochran's 1994 public artwork — 109 six-foot white concrete ears of corn standing in rows in a Dublin park, a tribute to farmer Sam Frantz and the area's agricultural roots. Free.

    4995 Rings Rd, Dublin, OH 43017

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Atlas Obscura, COLUMBUSMAKESART, WOSU Public Media

  3. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Dublin Link

    The world's longest single-tower S-shaped suspension bridge (760 ft, opened 2020) — a curving pedestrian span whose deck threads the keyhole of a 169-ft tower, linking Historic Dublin to Riverside Crossing Park. Free.

    6625 Riverside Dr, Dublin, OH 43017

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia, Columbus Underground

  4. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Inniswood Metro Gardens

    A 123-acre metro park of themed display gardens in Westerville — herb, rose and woodland gardens, a Sisters' Garden and boardwalk nature trails through nature preserve. Free.

    940 S Hempstead Rd, Westerville, OH 43081

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Wikipedia, Experience Columbus

  5. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Early Television Museum

    A 6,000-sq-ft Hilliard oddity holding 150+ working sets — mechanical 1920s scanning-disc TVs, prewar and early-color receivers — one of the world's deepest early-television collections. Free (donations welcome), weekends only.

    Your guide’s note Free; open Sat 10–6 and Sun 12–5.

    5396 Franklin St, Hilliard, OH 43026

    Recommended by Official site, Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia

  6. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Anti-Saloon League Museum

    Inside the Westerville library, in the League's old printing-plant town — 'the dry capital of the world' — the nation's foremost temperance/Prohibition collection: propaganda, artifacts and the story of the Ohio-born movement that drove the 18th Amendment. Free.

    Your guide’s note Free; open library hours or by appointment.

    126 S State St, Westerville, OH 43081

    Recommended by Official site, Ohio Magazine, Atlas Obscura

  7. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Hayden Run Falls

    A 35-foot ravine waterfall in Dublin, reached by a short wheelchair-accessible boardwalk and staircase in Columbus's two-acre Hayden Falls Nature Preserve — best after rain. Free, distinct from Dublin's Indian Run Falls.

    Look for Free; open daily 6am–10pm.

    4326 Hayden Run Rd, Dublin, OH 43017

    Recommended by Official site, Visit Dublin Ohio (CVB), Columbus Navigator

  8. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Easton Town Center

    A 30-million-visitor-a-year open-air 'town' laid out like a 1950s Main Street — 250+ shops from Nordstrom to Louis Vuitton alongside restaurants, cinemas and free public events. Repeatedly named the top retail experience in America. A tourism draw in its own right.

    160 Easton Town Center, Columbus, OH 43219

    Recommended by Official site, Experience Columbus, Wikipedia

  9. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Highbanks Metro Park

    A 1,200-acre metro park north of the city named for its 100-ft shale bluffs over the Olentangy River — ten trails, a nature center, a sledding hill and ancient Adena burial mounds. Free.

    9466 Columbus Pike, Lewis Center, OH 43035

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Wikipedia

  10. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    AMA Motorcycle Hall of Fame Museum

    The American Motorcyclist Association's national museum in Pickerington — vintage and racing motorcycles and the Hall of Fame honoring the sport's legends.

    13515 Yarmouth Dr, Pickerington, OH 43147

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia

  11. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Sharon Woods Metro Park

    A 761-acre Metro Park wrapping the 11-acre Schrock Lake and the Edward S. Thomas State Nature Preserve, with old-growth oak-hickory-beech woods and a 3.8-mile paved multipurpose loop. Free.

    6911 Cleveland Ave, Westerville, OH 43081

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Experience Columbus

  12. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Blendon Woods Metro Park

    A 653-acre Metro Park whose 118-acre Walden Waterfowl Refuge and 11-acre Thoreau Lake draw hundreds of birds — 220+ species logged — viewed from two elevated shelters with spotting scopes. Free.

    4265 E Dublin-Granville Rd, Westerville, OH 43081

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Experience Columbus

  13. Worth the detour · Suburbs

    Slate Run Living Historical Farm

    An 1880s working farm inside Slate Run Metro Park — costumed staff tend heirloom pigs, geese, turkeys and Percheron horses and cook in an 1856 Gothic-revival farmhouse, recreating daily central-Ohio farm life. Free.

    Your guide’s note Free; seasonal hours (open Tue–Sun; closed some winter days).

    1375 State Route 674 N, Canal Winchester, OH 43110

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Ohio Magazine

  14. Worth the detour · Soul, BBQ & Southern · Suburbs

    City Barbeque — Upper Arlington

    The original City Barbeque, founded in Columbus in 1999 in a former doughnut shop by a team that won the American Royal Invitational for best brisket — the recipe that grew a Columbus-born pit-BBQ chain.

    2111 W Henderson Rd, Columbus, OH 43220

    Recommended by Columbus Underground, Wikipedia

  15. Deep cut · Suburbs

    The Wagnalls Memorial

    A storybook 1925 Tudor Gothic library and cultural center in tiny Lithopolis, gifted by Mabel Wagnalls (of Funk & Wagnalls) in memory of her parents — stone, stained glass and a theater.

    150 E Columbus St, Lithopolis, OH 43136

    Recommended by Official site, Wikipedia, Ohio Magazine

  16. Deep cut · Suburbs

    Indian Run Falls

    A wooded ravine steps from Historic Dublin with a multi-tier waterfall dropping into Indian Run — boardwalks, viewing decks and a short trail named for its Wyandot campsite history. Free.

    700 Shawan Falls Dr, Dublin, OH 43017

    Recommended by Visit Dublin Ohio (CVB), Columbus Navigator

  17. Deep cut · Suburbs

    Orange Johnson House

    One of Worthington's oldest homes — an 1811 pioneer house with an 1816 Federal addition, restored by the Worthington Historical Society to show early-19th-century village life.

    956 High St, Worthington, OH 43085

    Recommended by Official site, Ohio.org (Ohio state tourism)

  18. Deep cut · Suburbs

    Hanby House

    The 1850s Westerville home of the Hanby family — Bishop William Hanby, an Underground Railroad conductor and Otterbein co-founder, and son Benjamin, composer of 'Up on the Housetop' and abolitionist ballad 'Darling Nelly Gray.'

    160 W Main St, Westerville, OH 43081

    Recommended by Westerville Historical Society, Visit Westerville (CVB)

Madison County 3

London, West Jefferson

  1. Must see · American & New American · Madison County

    The Red Brick Tavern

    A genuine National Road landmark still serving dinner — built 1836–37 in Lafayette and reputed to be Ohio's second-oldest stagecoach inn, host to six U.S. presidents (subject of an Ohio Historical Marker and National Road travel histories). Known today for prime rib and home-cooked specials. Open Tue–Sat (active listings, Aug 2026). Merit is the landmark itself; food is honest tavern fare.

    1700 Cumberland St, London, OH 43140

    Recommended by The Historical Marker Database, TOURINGOHIO, NATLROADBLOG

  2. Worth the detour · Madison County

    Red Brick Tavern

    A landmark 1836-37 National Road stagecoach inn in tiny Lafayette, said to be second only to the Golden Lamb among Ohio's oldest continuously recognized taverns; it hosted six U.S. presidents. Documented by the Library of Congress HABS survey. Closed 2020, reopened Feb 2023 and still operating as a historic tavern you can walk into.

    1700 Cumberland St (US-40), Lafayette, OH 43140

    Recommended by Library of Congress (HABS survey), The Historical Marker Database, Official site

  3. Worth the detour · Madison County

    Prairie Oaks Metro Park

    A 2,200-acre Metro Park straddling the Madison-Franklin line along Big Darby Creek (a state and national scenic river), with restored prairie, quarry-pond beaches and paddling, and prime birding. The Madison County side lies west of the creek. Distinct from Battelle Darby Creek downstream.

    3225 Plain City-Georgesville Rd, West Jefferson, OH 43162

    Recommended by Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks, Birding in Ohio (eBird hotspot atlas)

62 sights and 24 places to eat across Columbus and its neighborhoods, each traceable to the source that named it. The city’s food is a sleeper great — Jeni’s ice cream (born here), the North Market, Columbus-style square-cut pizza, Schmidt’s German cream puffs and one of America’s deepest Somali tables.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Columbus’s signature strength is range: Jeni’s Splendid ice cream (born here), the North Market, Columbus-style square-cut pizza, Schmidt’s German sausage & cream puffs, and one of the largest Somali tables in the US, sourced to the Columbus Dispatch, Columbus Monthly and Columbus Underground. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, Eater SF, The Infatuation, SF Chronicle, Mercury News, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json (direct map/page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open.
